title: How a program runs
objective: Explain what a program is, run one, and read a simple error message.

explanation.text: A **program** is a list of instructions for the computer. You write the instructions in a language such as Python. Python reads them **from top to bottom, one line at a time**, and does what each line says.

Writing the program is not enough. You must **run** it. In this page you press the **Run** button. On your own computer you type `python my_file.py` in a terminal. Both do the same thing: Python reads your file and follows it.

Computers do exactly what you write, not what you mean. If a line has a mistake, Python stops and shows an **error message**. This is normal. Every programmer sees errors every day, and the message tells you what to fix.

items: The **last line** of the message names the kind of error and says what is wrong.
The lines above say **where**: the line number of your code.
Read the message, look at that line, and fix one thing at a time.

explanation.text: An error does not mean you broke anything. Nothing is damaged. Fix the line and press Run again.

lines.explain: The first instruction. `print` shows the text on the screen. Python does this one first.
Python goes down to the next line only when the line above is finished.
The last line. When it is done, the program ends.

examples.title: What an error looks like (read only)
examples.code:
print("Hello)
SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 1)

The last line says what is wrong: a quote was opened but never closed.

exercises.prompt:
This program makes tea, but the steps are in the wrong order. Change the order of the lines so that it prints:

```
Boil water
Put tea in the cup
Add the water
Wait
Drink
```
exercises.starterCode:
print("Add the water")
print("Drink")
print("Boil water")
print("Wait")
print("Put tea in the cup")

tests.output:
Boil water
Put tea in the cup
Add the water
Wait
Drink

hints: Python runs the lines from top to bottom, so the order of the lines is the order of the output.
Move the lines, or retype them in the right order.
exercises.solution:
print("Boil water")
print("Put tea in the cup")
print("Add the water")
print("Wait")
print("Drink")

exercises.prompt:
Print this small box. Type it exactly, with the same spaces:

```
+-----+
| Hi! |
+-----+
```
hints: Everything between the quotes is printed as it is, including spaces.

debug.title: A quote that never closes
debug.symptom: SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 1)
debug.prompt: Fix the code so that it prints `Hello`.
hints: Text needs a quote at the start **and** at the end.
Add the missing `"` before the bracket.

debug.title: A misspelled name
debug.symptom: NameError: name 'Print' is not defined. Did you mean: 'print'?
debug.prompt: Fix the code so that it prints `Hi`.
hints: Python cares about capital letters. `Print` and `print` are different names.

mistakes.why: Python treats capital and small letters as different, so it does not know the name.

mistakes.mistake: Forgetting a closing quote or bracket.
mistakes.why: Python reads on, cannot find the end, and reports a `SyntaxError`.
mistakes.fix: Count your quotes and brackets. Each one that opens must close.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting Python to understand what you mean.
mistakes.why: The computer only follows the exact instructions.
mistakes.fix: Write each step clearly, in the order you want it to happen.

mistakes.mistake: Changing many things at once after an error.
mistakes.why: You cannot tell which change fixed it, or broke something else.
mistakes.fix: Fix one thing, run again, and read the new message.

quiz.question: In what order does Python run the lines of a program?
options: From top to bottom, one at a time
quiz.explanation: Python follows the lines in the order you wrote them.

quiz.question: Where is the most useful line of an error message?
quiz.explanation: The last line names the error and says what is wrong.

quiz.question: What should you do when Python shows an error?
options: Read the message and fix that line
quiz.explanation: Errors are normal. The message tells you where to look.

challenge.title: A tiny timetable
challenge.prompt:
Print a timetable with these three lines, in this order:

```
Monday: Python
Tuesday: Practice
Wednesday: Rest
```
challenge.stretch: Add a fourth line for Thursday and Friday.

tests.output:
Monday: Python
Tuesday: Practice
Wednesday: Rest

hints: The colon and the space after it are part of the text.
challenge.solution:
print("Monday: Python")
print("Tuesday: Practice")
print("Wednesday: Rest")
